name: San Francisco
tagline: Fog-kissed hills, clanging cable cars and a bridge glowing in the mist
description:
San Francisco crams astonishing variety into its famous seven-by-seven-mile footprint. One minute you're gripping the brass pole of a cable car as it crests a hill and the bay opens up below; the next you're in a Chinatown alley scented with roast duck and incense, or sipping espresso in the North Beach cafés where Beat poets once argued until dawn. On summer afternoons, fog pours through the Golden Gate and swallows the bridge's red towers, and locals simply pull on another layer.

Each neighborhood has its own personality. The Mission hums with murals, taquerias and natural-wine bars, the Castro wears its rainbow-flag history proudly, and the Haight still flickers with psychedelic nostalgia. Out west, Golden Gate Park rolls three miles to a wild Pacific beach where surfers brave cold, heavy swells.

Come hungry. Sourdough, Dungeness crab and cioppino carry the city's maritime roots, while farm-to-table cooking is practically a civic religion, fed by the valleys and coastline just beyond. Prices run high and the weather is famously moody, but ride a ferry beneath the bridge, climb a hilltop staircase at sunset or cross the bay to the hushed redwoods of Muir Woods, and it all feels worth it.

safety.notes: Car break-ins are extremely common, so never leave anything visible in a parked car, even for five minutes. Parts of the Tenderloin and SoMa near Sixth Street can feel rough, especially after dark; stick to busy streets and use a rideshare late at night.

tipping: Tip 18–22% at restaurants; many bills also carry a 4–6% health or staffing surcharge, which goes to the business and is not a substitute for the tip.
gettingAround: Muni buses, streetcars and cable cars cover the city while BART links the airport, downtown and the Mission; tap a Clipper card or contactless bank card to ride. The hills are brutally steep, so plan walks with a map and let transit do the climbing.
tips: Pack layers even in July: a sunny 75°F afternoon in the Mission can be a foggy 55°F at Ocean Beach, and the wind on the Golden Gate Bridge is fierce.
Book Alcatraz tickets through the official ferry operator two to four weeks ahead; third-party resellers charge more for the same boat.
A 1-, 3- or 7-day Muni Visitor Passport covers unlimited cable cars, buses and streetcars and pays for itself after two cable car rides.
Board the cable car a few stops up the line rather than at the Powell and Market turnaround, where the queue can top an hour on weekends.
BART from SFO to downtown takes about 30 minutes and costs around $10, usually beating a rideshare stuck in freeway traffic.
Hit the Ferry Building farmers market on a Saturday before 10 a.m., then eat your haul on the waterfront benches facing the Bay Bridge.
etiquette: Call it SF or 'the City'; 'Frisco' and 'San Fran' make locals wince.
Sort your waste: compost, recycling and landfill bins are everywhere, and people notice if you mix them.
Bring a reusable bag, since shops charge for bags at checkout.
Dress is casual even at high-end restaurants; a hoodie and sneakers rarely raise an eyebrow.

neighborhoods.name: Mission District
neighborhoods.blurb: The city's sunniest pocket, alive with Latino heritage, vivid alley murals, taquerias, natural-wine bars and weekend crowds sprawled across Dolores Park.

neighborhoods.name: North Beach
neighborhoods.blurb: San Francisco's Little Italy, where old espresso bars, Beat Generation bookshops and red-sauce trattorias sit beneath Telegraph Hill and Coit Tower.

neighborhoods.name: Haight-Ashbury
neighborhoods.blurb: Birthplace of the 1967 Summer of Love, still colorful with vintage and record shops, painted Victorians and easy access to Golden Gate Park.

neighborhoods.name: Hayes Valley
neighborhoods.blurb: A compact, stylish enclave of independent boutiques, design stores, beer gardens and a leafy central park strip near the opera and symphony.

neighborhoods.name: The Castro
neighborhoods.blurb: One of the world's most famous LGBTQ+ neighborhoods, crowned by a glorious 1920s movie palace and buzzing with bars, brunch spots and rainbow crosswalks.

dishes.name: Mission burrito
dishes.description: An oversized flour tortilla packed with rice, beans, grilled meat and salsa, then wrapped in foil; order it 'super' for cheese, sour cream and guacamole.

dishes.name: Cioppino
dishes.description: A fisherman's stew born on the wharves, loaded with crab, clams, mussels and fish in a garlicky tomato-wine broth, served with sourdough for dunking.

dishes.name: Clam chowder in a sourdough bowl
dishes.description: Creamy New England-style chowder ladled into a hollowed-out loaf of tangy local sourdough, best on a foggy waterfront afternoon.

dishes.name: Dungeness crab
dishes.description: Sweet, meaty local crab in season from roughly November to June, served cracked and chilled, roasted with garlic or tossed into salads.

dishes.name: Dim sum
dishes.description: Bite-sized Cantonese dumplings, buns and rolls, from shrimp har gow to barbecue-pork bao, eaten with tea at breakfast or lunch.

events.name: Chinese New Year Festival and Parade
events.description: One of the largest Lunar New Year celebrations outside Asia, with a nighttime parade of illuminated floats, firecrackers and a block-long golden dragon.

events.name: Bay to Breakers
events.description: A gloriously weird 12K footrace from the bay to Ocean Beach, where elite runners share the course with costumed revelers and moving parties.

events.name: San Francisco Pride
events.description: A massive parade down Market Street and a weekend of parties and celebrations across the Castro and Civic Center.

events.name: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass
events.description: A free, multi-stage weekend of roots, folk and bluegrass music in the meadows of Golden Gate Park.

attractions.name: Golden Gate Bridge
attractions.description: Painted a rusty orange so it stands out in the fog, the bridge's Art Deco towers rise 746 feet above the churning mouth of the bay. Walk the east sidewalk for salt spray and sweeping views back to the city, then continue to Battery Spencer on the Marin side for the classic postcard angle.
attractions.bookingTip: Arrive by 9 a.m. or take Muni bus 28 to the toll plaza, since the small Welcome Center lot fills quickly on weekends.

attractions.name: Alcatraz Island
attractions.description: Once home to America's most notorious convicts, the island prison sits a brisk ferry ride from the waterfront, its crumbling cellblocks and wild gardens now cared for by the National Park Service. The audio tour, narrated by former guards and inmates, brings escape attempts and riots vividly to life.
attractions.hours: Ferries from Pier 33 roughly 08:45–16:00 daily; evening tours on select days
attractions.bookingTip: Tickets sell only through the official ferry operator and often run out two to four weeks ahead; the night tour is the most atmospheric.

attractions.name: Golden Gate Park
attractions.description: Bigger than New York's Central Park, this three-mile ribbon of green hides a Victorian glasshouse full of orchids, a serene Japanese tea garden, a bison paddock and two major museums. Rent a bike and ride west through eucalyptus groves until the park ends at the roaring Pacific.
attractions.bookingTip: The eastern stretch of JFK Drive is permanently car-free, making it ideal for bikes, skates and strollers any day of the week.

attractions.name: Ferry Building
attractions.description: The clock-towered 1898 ferry terminal is now the city's gourmet pantry, lined with cheesemakers, oyster bars, bakers, mushroom growers and chocolatiers. On market days, farmers pile the plaza outside with heirloom tomatoes, stone fruit and just-picked greens.
attractions.hours: 07:00–20:00 daily; farmers market Tue, Thu & Sat
attractions.bookingTip: Come on Saturday before 10 a.m. for the full farmers market, then picnic on the bayside benches behind the building.

attractions.name: Chinatown
attractions.description: North America's oldest Chinatown is a dense grid of red lanterns, herbal apothecaries, temple balconies and bakeries turning out egg tarts by the tray. Pass through the Dragon Gate onto Grant Avenue, then slip into the side alleys where mahjong tiles click behind half-open doors.
attractions.bookingTip: Visit on a weekday morning, when locals shop for produce along Stockton Street and the dim sum counters are at their freshest.

attractions.name: Coit Tower
attractions.description: This fluted concrete tower atop Telegraph Hill hides a surprise at its base: sweeping Depression-era murals of California workers, farms and city life. Ride the tiny elevator for a 360-degree panorama of both bridges and the bay, and listen for the wild parrots squawking in the surrounding gardens.
attractions.bookingTip: Skip the scarce parking and climb up via the garden-lined Filbert Steps from the Embarcadero side.

attractions.name: San Francisco Cable Cars
attractions.description: The world's last manually operated cable car system still clangs up and over the steepest hills, with gripmen hauling levers and riders hanging off the running boards. The Powell–Hyde line serves the best views, cresting Russian Hill with Alcatraz framed dead ahead before dropping toward the bay.
attractions.bookingTip: Dodge the long queue at the Powell and Market turnaround by boarding a few stops up the line, or ride the quieter California Street route.

attractions.name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
attractions.wiki: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
attractions.description: Seven floors of modern and contemporary art, from Rothko and Warhol to Calder mobiles and groundbreaking photography, fill a striking rippled white building in SoMa. The free ground-floor galleries and the lush living wall on the third-floor terrace are worth a stop even when time is short.
attractions.bookingTip: Book a timed slot online and start on the top floor, working your way down ahead of the midday crowds.

attractions.name: Muir Woods National Monument
attractions.description: Under an hour north of the Golden Gate, cathedral-like groves of coast redwoods, some taller than 250 feet and many centuries old, tower over a murmuring creek. Flat boardwalk loops suit all ages, while the Ben Johnson Trail climbs away from the crowds into mossy silence.
attractions.bookingTip: Every private car needs an advance parking reservation, or book the seasonal shuttle; nobody gets in without one.

attractions.name: Mission Dolores
attractions.description: The thick-walled adobe chapel, completed in 1791, is the oldest intact building in San Francisco, its ceiling decorated with Ohlone designs painted in vegetable dyes. The small cemetery garden and the ornate basilica next door are a quiet counterpoint to the buzzing Mission District outside.
attractions.bookingTip: Pair it with a picnic in Dolores Park two blocks south, which is often the sunniest lawn in the city.

hotels.name: The Nob Crest
hotels.description: Perched on the summit of Nob Hill where cable cars clang past the door, this grand dame pairs 1920s marble lobbies with rooms dressed in fog-grey silk and brushed brass. The top-floor lounge looks over rooftops to both bridges, and the eucalyptus steam room cures any jet lag.

hotels.name: Panhandle Poppy House
hotels.description: A lovingly restored 1890s Victorian painted poppy orange and sage, with bay-windowed rooms, clawfoot tubs and a wine-and-cheese hour in the front parlor. The park's eastern edge is a five-minute walk, perfect for morning runs to the Conservatory of Flowers.

hotels.name: Barbary Coast Bunks
hotels.description: Dorm bunks with reading lights and lockers above a row of North Beach cafés, plus a big shared kitchen, free pancake breakfasts and a roof deck facing Coit Tower. Nightly walks through the old Barbary Coast saloon district make friends fast.

hotels.name: Tidewire Hotel
hotels.nearAttraction: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
hotels.description: A sleek glass-and-cedar tower with rotating installations by Bay Area artists, rain showers, smart-glass privacy walls and a lobby that doubles as a coworking lounge. SFMOMA and Yerba Buena Gardens are a two-minute walk.

hotels.name: The Wharfinger House
hotels.description: Built in 1911 as a harbor master's office and seamen's lodge, this brick waterfront building now offers rooms with exposed timber, ship-lantern lighting and windows onto the Bay Bridge. The breakfast room gets first pick from the farmers market next door.

hotels.name: Valencia Street Flats
hotels.description: Bright one- and two-bedroom apartments above a row of Mission storefronts, each with a full kitchen, washer-dryer and bikes to borrow. Dolores Park's lawns, often the warmest spot in the city, are a short stroll away.

restaurants.name: Jackson Alley Dumpling House
restaurants.description: A steamy, no-frills takeout counter where aunties pleat har gow and siu mai in the window and bamboo steamers stack toward the ceiling. Point at whatever looks good, pay in cash and eat on a bench in nearby Portsmouth Square.
restaurants.signatureDish: Har gow shrimp dumplings and baked char siu bao

restaurants.name: Taquería Paloma Brava
restaurants.description: Foil-wrapped burritos the size of your forearm, carne asada seared on a roaring flat-top and a salsa bar with six house-made heat levels. Order it super and grab a seat at the long communal tables under the neon.

restaurants.name: Caffè Telegrafo
restaurants.description: An old-school espresso bar with a marble counter, opera crackling on the stereo and rosemary focaccia pulled from the oven each morning. Fuel up here before climbing the stairways to Coit Tower.

restaurants.name: Cypress & Tide
restaurants.nearAttraction: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
restaurants.description: A serene room of pale oak and hand-thrown ceramics where a twelve-course menu follows the Northern California coast from tide pool to redwood ridge. Wine pairings spotlight tiny Sonoma and Mendocino producers you won't find on other lists.
restaurants.signatureDish: Dungeness crab with Meyer lemon and sea lettuce

restaurants.name: Tidewater Cioppino House
restaurants.description: The cioppino arrives in a cast-iron pot brimming with crab, clams and rockfish in a garlicky tomato broth, with a loaf of sourdough for mopping. Book a window table to watch the Bay Bridge lights flicker on.

restaurants.name: Shwe Lotus Burmese Kitchen
restaurants.description: Neighborhood regulars queue for the fermented tea leaf salad, tossed tableside with crunchy fried beans, peanuts and sesame, and for fragrant coconut-chicken noodle soup. It's a cuisine San Francisco does better than almost anywhere outside Myanmar.

restaurants.name: Columbus & Vallejo Trattoria
restaurants.description: Checkered tablecloths, candles in straw-wrapped Chianti bottles and a waiter who will insist you order the clams. Handmade pasta and a smart list of California-grown Italian grape varieties make it a warm, lively dinner stop.
restaurants.signatureDish: Linguine with clams, garlic and white wine

restaurants.name: Hyde & Clay
restaurants.description: A candlelit corner bistro on the cable car line serving wood-fired chicken, farmers-market vegetables and a tight list of natural wines by the glass. The bar seats are a great perch for solo travelers.
restaurants.signatureDish: Wood-fired chicken with farro and Meyer lemon

experiences.name: Golden Gate Ride & Sausalito Ferry
experiences.description: Pedal across the Golden Gate on a quality e-bike with a guide who knows every photo stop, then coast down to Sausalito's houseboat harbor for lunch. The return ferry slides past Alcatraz and drops you back on the city waterfront.

experiences.name: Chinatown Alleys & Dim Sum Walk
experiences.description: Duck into a fortune cookie workshop, an herbal apothecary and a hidden rooftop temple with a guide who grew up above a Chinatown bakery. Tastings include egg tarts, roast pork, hand-pulled noodles and a proper sit-down dim sum lunch.

experiences.name: Redwood Forest Bathing & Tea
experiences.description: A slow, guided sensory walk beneath centuries-old coast redwoods, with breathing pauses, creekside journaling and no pressure to cover distance. It ends with herbal tea served on a quiet trail spur, far from the boardwalk crowds.

experiences.name: Mission Murals & Mezcal Night
experiences.description: Start with the vivid murals of Balmy and Clarion alleys at golden hour, then hop between three Mission bars for a mezcal flight, craft cocktails and a late-night taco stop. Your guide is a working muralist who knows the stories behind every wall.
